description: Production monitoring of MaaS, Praxis, their in-cluster PostgreSQL dependency and cluster resources handling real end-user traffic, with collection health, tenant/route views and metric explorers. Metric names and labels were confirmed from September 30, 2026 historical data; current collection health must be checked in the dashboard.

options.content:
**Production scope:** MaaS, Praxis, their in-cluster dependencies and the underlying cluster resources handling real end-user traffic. Praxis upstream request, error and timing metrics describe observations made by the in-cluster service. HTTP request rates do not establish client-confirmed response completion or session counts.

**Application metrics:** select EnMaaS Prometheus. **Platform metrics:** select OpenShift Thanos / platform Prometheus. The application source federates only `node_*`; pod/container panels need the platform source. Default namespace is **enmaas**. Datasource selections are visible and no credentials are embedded.

**Scope:** Tenant filters MaaS HTTP/key/token metrics. Praxis cluster filters cluster-labeled gateway metrics; Praxis route filters HTTP request counts and latency only. Active requests, errors, header duration and unlabelled MaaS counters remain service-wide. Pod and Node instance control resource panels; Explorer job controls the application metric catalog.

**Collection first:** missing/down targets cannot produce current traffic metrics. The status cards below distinguish **UP**, **DOWN**, and **NO TARGET** at the selected time-range end. A zero-filled rate is never substituted for missing application data. Details and metric catalogs are collapsed to limit query load. Application metrics were confirmed in historical samples on September 30; see the dated inspection notes for the collection problems observed then.

**Explorer job** and **Application metric** discover names from the application source within the selected time range. The inventory includes series observed anywhere in that window, even if scraping is now down. The raw-value chart shows historical samples; the current table evaluates at the range end and can therefore be empty during an outage. Select a pre-outage time window when investigating earlier data.

Every scraped namespace/job metric is discoverable, including PostgreSQL and metering if collected. Raw values are not automatically converted to rates. The chart is limited to 50 series; the label table is unaggregated. The explorer intentionally ignores Tenant and Praxis filters so it can show the full metric contract. Set namespace to `cnpg-system` to inspect the operator. Missing metering instrumentation or an undiscovered job cannot be fixed by a dashboard.

options.content:
### Confirmed metric evidence — September 30, 2026
The previous read-only inspection queried standalone EnMaaS Prometheus and OpenShift Thanos. MaaS/Praxis metric names and label keys were obtained from the last-24-hour series catalog and confirmed against **14:55 UTC (10:55 a.m. Eastern)** samples. Token minting appeared in the catalog but not that instant snapshot. Additional metric semantics are called out where unverified. This dashboard update itself made **no cluster connection or change**.

### Collection problems observed around 14:57–14:59 UTC
- MaaS (`9090`), Praxis (`9901`) and PostgreSQL (`9187`) scrape targets reported timeouts; all last showed success shortly before new NetworkPolicies appeared at **14:56:26–27 UTC**.
- The policies excluded ingress from `enmaas-monitoring`. The Praxis monitoring exception selected `openshift-monitoring`, a different namespace.
- The Praxis scrape annotation specified `9901`, while its Service exposed only `8081` and `8084`; the pod still declared `9901`.
- These are **dated observations**, not assertions of current state. Use the live collection cards to see whether collection has recovered. No policy, Service, scrape configuration, or ServiceMonitor was changed by this dashboard work.
- There were no MaaS/Praxis ServiceMonitors or PodMonitors. EnMaaS Prometheus used annotated Service discovery. Metering had no scrape annotation.

### Datasources and filters
- **Application metrics:** existing EnMaaS Prometheus. **Platform metrics:** existing OpenShift Thanos/platform Prometheus. The former federated only node metrics; the latter was verified to contain container CPU/memory/throttling, requests/limits, pod readiness, PVC usage and node metrics.
- Import prompts map these two sources; pickers remain visible. This JSON creates no datasource and embeds no token. Each source should be scoped to one cluster or filtered to this cluster.
- Tenant filters only tenant-labeled MaaS HTTP/key/token metrics. Praxis cluster filters cluster-labeled metrics; Praxis route filters HTTP request counts and durations. All other panels explicitly state their service-wide scope. Explorer job applies only to the application catalog.
- Set the application datasource scrape interval to **30s**. Panel minimum query step is 30s and rates use `$__rate_interval`. Default refresh is 30s. Pause refresh for historical analysis; label variables rediscover their options when the time range changes.

### Interpretation
- Service-based scraping can combine different backend replicas under one instance label. Per-replica totals, runtime gauges and summaries may therefore jump between pods. Fleet percentiles and PostgreSQL replica health are not established by those series.
- MaaS latency uses histogram buckets. Praxis latency/connection/header summaries remain separate by complete label set; do not average summary quantiles. Duration sum/count can provide a mean. Exporter-summary windows are independent of the Grafana time range.
- Praxis HTTP requests are separated from upstream attempts; retries can make their counts differ. `praxis_errors_total` has a type label and is service-wide. Its ratio to upstream attempts is diagnostic, not an availability SLO.
- No pass/fail acceptance threshold, 30-day SLO verdict, or successful-zero fallback is invented. Metric-presence probes deliberately display Missing; scrape cards deliberately display NO TARGET for absent up series.
- CPU is in cores, memory/body sizes in bytes, latency in seconds, resource utilization in percent. Request rates use the rate window; totals and restarts use the entire selected window. Unset limits, missing label series, idle traffic and unavailable optional exporters can yield empty panels.
- PostgreSQL panels retain actual labels rather than assuming database/role label names. Cumulative database statistics are shown raw where exporter type was not independently verified. Service scraping does not expose all three database replicas separately.

### Artifact format
Grafana Classic JSON, schemaVersion 39, matching the existing quickstart format. All changes are local to `dashboard.json`; no Grafana import was performed.
